headline: Single-cell and bulk transcriptomics define malignant states and therapeutic candidates
label: Multi Omics Cancer Transcriptomic Modeling
summary: Public perturbation atlases, patient-level cohorts and transferable classifiers now resolve cancer cell states at greater scale and resolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the integration of single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomics with computational modeling to define malignant states and prioritize therapeutic candidates. Tahoe-100M profiles 100 million single-cell transcriptomes across 50 cancer cell lines and 1,100 drug-dose conditions, and Cell-Sign uses a simple classifier to detect drug treatment and exposure duration in scRNA-seq data. Other studies apply comparable logic to patient stratification, including five malignant archetypes in large B cell lymphoma linked to poor event-free survival, a sialylation-based index for HNSCC, and an ATXN2-linked stress granule transcript program in colorectal cancer. TISON extends patient-specific network modeling to drug scoring, and surfaceome profiling in acute leukemia targets cell-surface immunotherapy candidates. What is new is the scale of perturbation data paired with transferable classifiers, though most items are retrospective reanalyses of public datasets.
